articleTitle: Development of ironless Halbach permanent magnet linear synchronous motor for traction of a novel maglev vehicle
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper presents the development of the single side ironless Halbach permanent magnet linear synchronous motor (PMLSM) for a novel electromagnetic suspension (EMS) maglev vehicle. The basic structure of the propulsion motor and the vehicle are firstly described. Then the thrust and normal force of the ironless PMLSM are analyzed. The configuration of the propulsion system and field oriented control (FOC) scheme of the motor are introduced. Single bogie prototype maglev vehicle have been developed and dynamic experiments have been performed on the 204m test line. The experimental results prove the feasibility of the motor for propulsion of the novel maglev vehicle.

articleTitle: Design analysis of a line-start permanent magnet linear synchronous motor
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: Characteristics of a line-start permanent magnet linear synchronous motor are presented. The motor is a surface permanent magnet synchronous motor with aluminum plate. It starts and accelerates as an induction motor and moves as a synchronous motor. Design analysis is performed. Basic characteristics in analysis using a finite element method are shown.

articleTitle: Maglev trends in public transport: The perspectives of Maglev transportation systems
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: The idea of considering Maglev systems challenges established ways of thinking on how to deal with an increasing transport demand. Today, the railway industry seems focused on traditional business models that profit from friction, wear and tear of established conventional transport systems. Maglev Systems have begun to challenge those traditional business concepts. Maglev is a fundamentally different concept of transport - which might explain the reluctance, even ignorance, which Maglev systems continue to face.

articleTitle: Development of high-acceleration linear motor system using the transient loss evaluation
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: For the purpose of the range expansion of the product which applied a linear motor, the examination of the linear motor realizing high acceleration drive progresses. In this situation, the importance of the evaluation of the linear motor for the acceleration region increases. This report describes the investigation that can evaluate performance of a linear motor at the transient state. The performance at the transient state is calculated by using control simulator and the FEM model. As a result of quantification, it was proved that the copper loss and the metal loss are dominant in all losses. Moreover we also described about the calculation results of comparison of different material plate on this method.

articleTitle: Study of linear vernier motor for household automatic doors
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: A DC brushless linear motor is used for household automatic doors. However, it has a problem that the cost is high due to a large amount of permanent magnets in the mover. In order to solve this problem, we have studied a linear vernier motor which permanent magnets are used only in the stator. In this paper, we compare the thrust characteristics of the vernier motor with those of conventional linear motors (DC brushless motors) using 3-D FEM.

articleTitle: Compact maglev motor with full DOF active control for miniaturized rotary blood pumps
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: Mechanical circulatory support using rotary ventricular assist devices (VADs) is one of the strongest therapy for heart disease patients. However, technical difficulties such as high mechanical durability, sufficient blood compatibility and small device size prevents VADs development for pediatric heart disease. In this study, an ultra-compact self-bearing motor whose diameter of 22 mm and height of 33 mm has been developed for durable and blood compatible centrifugal pediatric VADs. The motor employs a double stator mechanism using two identical motor stators to enhance torque production and achieve impeller suspension with an active 5-degrees of freedom (DOF) control. This paper investigated basic magnetic suspension performances of the developed self-bearing motor with the 5-DOF control. The motor achieved non-contact impeller suspension up to the rotating speed of 7500 rpm, and indicated sufficient magnetic suspension ability.

articleTitle: Design parameter analysis of the linear induction motor for Maglev conveying system
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper deals with an analysis of the design parameters and its influence on performance of the linear induction motor (LIM). LIM propels using Lorentz force generated by interaction between magnetic flux of the primary and eddy current induced in secondary. As depending on the size of the primary and the secondary, not only magnetic flux and induced eddy current, but also performances of the LIM are changed. In this paper, the thrust force, efficiency and power factor with various design parameters are analyzed by Finite Elements Method (FEM). The effect of design variables on objective functions is investigated by using Response Surface Method (RSM) and the optimal model that has improved thrust force, efficiency and power factor is derived.

articleTitle: Detent force reduction for a novel transverse flux permanent magnet linear synchronous motor without compromising stroke length
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: A novel configuration for reducing end-effect detent force for a high thrust transverse flux linear synchronous motor is presented. The method is based on principle of destructive superposition of harmonic orders in detent force waveform. It is achieved by splitting a linear motor, with a high slot-pole combination into three separate sections, allowing enhanced degree of freedom to mitigate end-effect harmonics without giving up the low slot-effect force feature of a high slot-pole structure. This splitting consequently increases available stroke length. Analytical and numerical analyses are conducted to verify the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Design of linear synchronous generator suitable for free-piston engine linear generator system
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: A free-piston engine linear generator (FPEG) system generates electricity using a linear generator when a free piston reciprocates the combustion thrust of the internal combustion. This system is expected to be applied to hybrid vehicles. In this paper, we propose a configuration for an FPEG, and we evaluate its static thrust and magnetic flux density distribution using finite element method (FEM) analysis.

articleTitle: Study on design method for thrust ripple reduction of double-sided linear switched reluctance motor
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper presents a thrust ripple reduction method for a double-sided linear switched reluctance motor (LSRM). A structure of motor is back-to-back mover LSRM. The spatial arrangement of the stator is investigated in order to reduce the thrust ripple. The thrust distribution generated by a phase of the LSRM is computed by finite element method (FEM) analysis. Based on numerical results of FEM analysis, the relationship between spatial arrangement of stator and thrust ripple is calculated. In the proposed thrust ripple reduction method, it is possible to reduce the thrust ripple without decreasing in an average thrust.

articleTitle: Performance improvement of a bearingless motor by rotation about an estimated center of inertia
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: Eccentric mass unbalance of the electric motor causes vibration of the shaft and the whole system, when the rotational speed increases. This paper considers rotation about an estimated center of inertia for a bearingless motor to reduce the vibration and power consumption for magnetic suspension. A 12-slot/10-pole bearingless SPM motor is selected for the performance test, because it has low suspension force ripple. The equation of motion for a bearingless motor with one-point mechanical support is derived. The mathematical model is derived to estimate the center of inertia. The prototype was built and tested, and the rotor rotates about an estimated center of inertia. The experimental results show effectiveness of the proposed method for performance improvement of the bearingless motor.

articleTitle: Active vibration control of drum type of washing machine using linear oscillatory actuator
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper proposes an evaluation method of vibration reduction for a linear oscillatory actuator using a fundamental frequency force. We have evaluated vibration reduction by the actuator through an experiment, but we did not evaluate it. Therefore we analyzed the frequency of the vibration waveform, and evaluated the vibration reduction of the first harmonic of the vibration waveform. As a result, the vibration reduction rate could be accurately evaluated. We analyzed the measured result, and we verified the effectiveness of active vibration control by the actuator.

articleTitle: Examination of a free-piston engine linear generator system with generation control for high efficiency
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: A free-piston engine linear generator system is investigated for use as a high-efficiency generator engine. The system's efficiency depends on its generation and thermal efficiency, and the generation efficiency is degraded at the edge of the expansion stroke when the piston speed is low and the thrust is high. The generation efficiency is thereby improved to 97% using machine coupling control. Furthermore, the system efficiency is increased to 46.5% using generation control to match the top dead center position with the theoretical ideal position during the compression stroke, which increases the thermal efficiency.

articleTitle: Modeling and experimental validation of field distributions due to eddy currents in slitted conducting plates
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: The paper describes a 3D semi-analytical harmonic modeling technique, which is capable to model eddy current distributions in conducting structures and the associated fields. The induced current density and magnetic fields in the spectral domain are described, where a spatially varying conductivity of a conducting region is incorporated in the solutions of magnetic-field quantities. An experimental setup is used to measure the field distribution above differently shaped conducting plates, placed on top of a coil, in which eddy currents are induced. The measurement results are compared to simulation results and the perturbations are analyzed.

articleTitle: Study of the effect of load torque on the iron losses of permanent magnet motors by finite element analysis
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: The output torque of an interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) can be controlled within its allowable range using a pulse-width modulation (PWM) inverter. In this paper, the effect of the load torque on the iron losses of an IPMSM is studied by investigating three driving conditions, namely no-current, no-load and load conditions. The experimental data demonstrates that a torque increase from 0 N·m to 1 N·m causes an iron loss increase of about 20 %. Three-dimensional (3D) finite element analysis (FEA) is performed and demonstrates that the magnet eddy current losses are the most affected by the torque increase.

articleTitle: Comparative study of two permanent magnet linear machines
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: Two permanent magnet linear machines, i.e. partitioned stator flux reversal permanent magnet (PS-FRPM) and conventional switched flux permanent magnet (SFPM) linear machines, are compared, in terms of electromagnetic performance and demagnetization withstand capability. It is found that compared to the conventional SFPM linear machine, the PS-FRPM linear machine shows lower cogging force, higher thrust force capability, better PM utilization, and lower thrust force ripple. Moreover, it possesses better demagnetization withstand capability.

articleTitle: Design analysis of a segment type linear switched reluctance motor
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: A segment type linear switched reluctance motor is proposed for a linear actuator or a liner generator. A flat gap motor and a cylindrical gap motor are designed and their characteristics are compared. The movers have concentrated armature windings. The stators consist of segment cores and aluminum block bodies. The characteristics are calculated using a finite element method analysis. The efficiency of the cylindrical gap motor is larger than the flat gap motor because the armature windings without end windings reduces copper loss.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of a partitioned stator flux reversal permanent magnet linear machine
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: Partitioned stator flux reversal permanent magnet (PS-FRPM) linear machine is a type of permanent magnet linear machine with dual active stators and one passive mover. Pervious work was shown that such a machine possesses the advantage of having big slot area leading to reduced phase resistance and consequently improved electric loading capability. In order to verify the finite element (FE) results, a prototype of PS-FRPM linear machine is built and tested. A comparison between the test and FE results is presented in this paper, together with the investigation on the influence of axial length differences.

articleTitle: Analysis of indirect field oriented control in long primary parallel-connected double-sided linear induction motor
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: The long primary double sided linear induction motor (DSLIM) has been used in many fields. The structure of parallel connected DSLIM is similar to multi-asynchronous motor fed by single inverter, but the control method is different due to the DSLIM parameters change. This paper analyses the characteristics of motor module in the operation condition of parallel connection, analyses the thrust fluctuation caused by the change of motor parameters in the movement. Then we propose a modified control scheme to restrain the fluctuation by increasing the exciting current and decreasing the thrust current. The simulation and experiments results verified the accuracy of analysis.

articleTitle: Precise positioning control of a linear induction motor drive system by utilizing nonlinear friction behaviors
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: In this paper, a new precise positioning control of a Linear Induction Motor (LIM) system guided by a linear ball bearing system is proposed. A coarse drive force resolution and slow response of the LIM can be overcome by a special control algorithm utilizing spring behaviors of the guide mechanism, therefore, the preciseness of positioning is effectively improved. Our proposed new control is a combination of the feedforward thrust force control based on the nonlinear spring characteristic of the guide and a usual PI-D control. The experiment showed the positioning resolution of the system is better than 2μm.

articleTitle: The study of parallel synchronous drive in Permanent magnet linear synchronous motor
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: In recently, permanent magnet type linear motors (PM-LSM) which could control high speed have attracted attention in the industrial field. Our laboratory is focusing on conveyance system. In the loading and unloading of the luggage of the transport system, the mover to move repeatedly to “stop-and-go”. This drive occurs each time to move the respective processing sections. This work leads to a reduction of transport efficiency. Therefore, we propose parallel synchronous drive. This method synchronizes the mover of the two LSMs. Because both movers in the synchronized state are the same inertia, luggage may be moved without the movers stop. Main line of the motor called “master motor” and another motor called “slave motor”. The master motor's position is passed Slave motor and parallel synchronous drive is run.

articleTitle: Stable magnetic levitation of 0.1-mm-thick steel plate as supreme thickness in our study
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: Adopting magnetic levitation techniques in Steel Processing Industries is a beneficial way in maintaining the high quality of steel's surfaces. However, the control for levitation and guidance is not so easy, because of difficulties in mechanical and magnetic characteristics of steel, especially in those of thin steel plates. We have already established the stable magnetic levitation and guidance control for 1.6mm-thick steel plates mainly. In this paper, we aim at stable magnetic levitation for a 0.1mm-thick steel plate, which thinness is our supreme target. In order to realize such a noncontact system for 0.1mm-thick steel plates, we have to take account of its vibration and its magnetic saturation and leakage. This paper will describe a methodology for stable magnetic levitation and guidance of 0.1mm-thick steel plates and show many successful experimental results by considering those difficult characteristics of very thin steel plates.

articleTitle: Magnetic field performance of round layout linear Halbach array using cylinder-shaped permanent magnets
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: The proposed Halbach array was constructed with eleven cylinder-shaped permanent magnets magnetized in the radial direction. In the proto-model of a Halbach array using cylindrical permanent magnets and synchronized rotation in the same direction of all magnets, the slide of the magnetic field distribution was confirmed by quasi-static measurement and simulation of magnetic field. In this report, we present round layout model of Halbach array having the characteristics of magnetic field control and constitutive flexibility and we show magnetic field distribution results by quasi-static measurement and magnetic field analysis.

articleTitle: Prediction and prevention of losing steps in a helical teethed linear actuator
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper describes the prediction and prevention of losing steps in helical teethed linear actuator (HTLA) for artificial muscle. When the rapid external force is applied to the HTLA, it becomes a state of losing steps. Therefore, it is important to predict and prevent this phenomenon. First, we clarified the phenomenon of losing steps in the HTLA by using numerical simulation with 3-D FEM. Next, we improved the force controller of the HTLA by adjusting of maximum current limit and two-degree-of-freedom PID control. As the results, the mover of the HTLA under the proposed controller was less likely to lose steps with respect to rapid external force and it was possible to improve the robustness for losing steps.

articleTitle: Improvement of the damping factor by the weight reduction damper coil in superconducting magnetically levitated bogie
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: Superconducting magnetically levitated transportation system has been developed. The electrodynamic suspension is used for levitation and guidance. Results of numerical simulation show that the damping factor of this EDS system is small. Thus the damper coil system is introduced to increase damping against oscillation of the bogie. This damper coil system has effect on decreasing oscillation of the bogie. However, because the weight of the damper coil is large, the energy loss increases. By changing the shape of the damper coil, the weight of the damper coil is reduced. In this paper, the running simulation of the bogie when the bogie passes the guideway displacement is undertaken. The weight reduction damper coil shows smaller the damping factor in the passive mode. But it shows larger the damping factor in the semi-active mode. The sufficient damping effect is shown by the weight reduction coil.

articleTitle: Investigation of single-sided ironless linear synchronous motor based on permanent magnet Halbach array used for medium-speed Maglev
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper investigates single-sided ironless linear synchronous motor (ILSM) based on permanent magnet Halbach array used for medium-speed maglev. Long primary ironless coil is laid along the track and the Halbach permanent magnet array is attached to the bottom of each bogie as a source of traction, two dimensional analytical model of single-sided ILSM is established used to calculate the characteristics of thrust and normal force against power angle, thrust force reach maximum meanwhile normal force can be eliminated when power angle is 90°, The accuracy of the calculation is verified by finite element calculate and experiment. Besides, the mathematical model of this type motor is built by 3D finite element method, thus the traction characteristics of medium-speed maglev under maximum speed 200km/h can be calculated, including current, voltage, efficiency curves, etc. some important conclusions are obtained.

articleTitle: Local magnetic characteristics of electrical motor core by magnetic hysteresis analysis with inverter excitation
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: We obtain local B-H characteristics on an electrical motor core under inverter excitation by using a 3-D magnetic hysteresis analysis. To obtain the local B-H characteristics leads to iron loss evaluation. In conventional research, a magnetic hysteresis analysis using 3-D model has hardly been performed for evaluation of the magnetic characteristics under inverter excitation. Therefore, this investigation shows the B-H characteristics. In addition, the local rotational magnetic field is also shown in this paper.

articleTitle: Iron loss characteristics under PWM inverter excitation at high ambient temperatures
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This study addresses magnetic properties of the inverter-fed electrical steel sheet under a wide range of ambient temperatures. We examine the iron loss characteristic under sinusoidal and inverter excitations at room temperature and 300 °C. The iron losses under sinusoidal and inverter excitations decrease with increasing temperatures because the electrical resistivity of electrical steel sheet increases. The temperature dependency of iron loss properties is related not only to major loops but also to minor loops in the B-H curve under inverter excitation.

articleTitle: Applications of linear machinery in public transport
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This short report deals with the application of linear machinery in public rail-guided transport. After summarizing advantages and disadvantages of linear motors, several examples of application of linear synchronous/induction motors in railways, including maglev applications<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>, are briefly described. Furthermore, the author explains recent efforts for international standardization of linear induction traction technology as well as for energy-saving automatic train operation at Japanese linear metros.

articleTitle: Considerations in the numerical design for the armatures of LIM-type eddy-current rail brakes
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: We have been developing LIM-type eddy current rail brakes (LIM-ECBs). In this paper, we introduced our approach to simplify the numerical design for the armatures of LIM-ECBs and show the study of changing the number of poles under fixed external dimensions as a specific example.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of a linear oscillatory actuator for active control engine mounts
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: A linear oscillatory actuator (LOA) for active control engine mounts (ACMs) is proposed in this paper. This LOA performs high thrust characteristics using a small size mover. Static and dynamic characteristics are computed through a coupled method of magnetic field and motion analyses employing 2-D finite element method. In addition, the effectiveness of proposed LOA is verified by the comparison with our previous LOA. In order to verify the applicability for an ACM system, vibration reductions using a least mean square adaptive filter are clarified.

articleTitle: Experimental confirmation of thrust and attractive force control for linear induction motor by two different frequency components
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: In this paper, a maglev transportation system with a Linear Induction Motor (LIM) is introduced. It is proposed that two different frequency components are used to achieve the simultaneous and independent control of the thrust and attractive force of LIM. One of the frequency components is synchronous with the motor speed (f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub>). The other frequency is drive frequency (f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sub>) that generates the thrust and attractive force. This proposed control method simplifies the design of the controller more easily, because the f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub> frequency component generates only an attractive force. Therefore, the controllers for thrust and attractive force can be separated and independent. This paper verifies the control performance of proposed system by the experimental results.

articleTitle: Increasing the force per unit volume of tubular drives by raising the integration degree
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper describes results elaborated by designing three different tubular linear drives for applications where hydraulic actuators are in common use. The superior force density of hydraulic actuators results in a challenging magnetic and mechanical design. However, electric-driven actuators offer advantages in dynamic behavior, controllability and efficiency.

articleTitle: Performance improvement of a linear permanent magnet gear
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper presents the design and analysis of high performance flat-type linear permanent magnet gears. A salient pole mover structure and a simple scheme of pole shift are proposed. Totally thirteen topologies (including those of the conventional topology and the twelve new topologies) with different mover structures are given. The corresponding prototypes with a gear ratio of −5.5:1 are optimally designed and comparatively analyzed with 2-D finite element analysis. The new prototypes have, more or less, improvement in thrust force performance and structure strength with the same usage of sintered NdFeB permanent magnets. Among them, five representative prototypes are analyzed in detail, in aspects of magnetic field distribution, flux density in airgaps, force-position characteristic and on-load thrust force analysis. Results indicate that the salient pole permanent magnet movers and the pole shift scheme are effective to improve the transmission force and the structure strength.

articleTitle: Dynamical model of an electromagnet by cauer ladder network representation of eddy-current fields
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamical modeling method for the magnetic actuators. The magnetic field is decomposed into orthogonal distribution functions by using continued fraction, which is equivalent to Cauer ladder network. The linearized transfer function of the magnetic force is derived by using theses distribution functions. Numerical example of electromagnet is also presented to show the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Improvement of average velocity error in the HTS magnetically levitated conveyance system
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: The magnetic levitation transport system is developed. In this system, by using the pinning force of the HTS, stable levitation and guide without control is realized. Propulsion force is generated by the interaction between the permanent magnet and the air core copper coil (propulsion coil). Since a larger propulsion force is required to improve the propulsion characteristics, the pinned flux of the HTS that maintains the carrier levitation is also used. In order to control the carrier velocity, the improved excitation method of the propulsion coil is introduced. The non-excitation mode coil is defined according to the velocity of the carrier. As a result, the average velocity error becomes smaller compared with that of the normal control method, and the propulsion characteristics are improved. Experimental results show that the average velocity error decreases by about 4.2%.

articleTitle: Influence of the HTS volume in the magnetic bearing using pinning effect
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: In flywheel system, rotor is supported by mechanical bearing. In the cases that the weight of the rotor is heavy and the rotational speed is high, mechanical loss is large. Superconducting magnetic bearing (SMB) is introduced to support with contact-less and control-less. The rotor is supported by the pinning effect in SMB. Pinning force depends on the specification of the HTS. In this paper, the dependence of the volume of the HTS for the pinning force is studied. The restoring force is measured when the load is added to the rotor. The vibration and the rotational speed are measured in the rotational motion. The area that the restoring force acts increases because the HTS surface is large. As results, the rotational vibration is suppressed. Therefore, the pinning characteristics greatly depend on the diameter of the HTS.

articleTitle: Zero-power control of flux-path control magnetic suspension system with flux-interrupting plates
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: The feasibility of zero-power control in flux-path control magnetic suspension is discussed. In the flux-path control magnetic suspension system, ferromagnetic control plates are inserted between a permanent magnet (magnetic source) and a floator and moved to vary the flux from the magnetic source to the floator. The zero-power control has been applied in active magnetic suspension with a DC electromagnet. In the zero-power controlled system, the control current was kept virtually zero in the steady states. The applicability of the zero-power control to the flux-path control magnetic suspension is discussed in this paper. The conditions required to achieve the zero-power control is presented in an analytical form. Experiments are carried in a fabricated apparatus to certify the theoretical predictions.

articleTitle: Technical challenges to realize energy-efficient linear metros in Japan
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: Subway operators introduced linear metros in 1990s and continued successful urban passenger transport service in many large and dense cities in Japan for more than a quarter century. A significant disadvantage of the linear metros is the relatively low energy efficiency. Therefore, Japan Subway Association (JSA) started a technical challenge to reduce the traction energy consumption of linear metros in 2012. After engineering efforts for three years, the improved automatic train operation (ATO) achieved the energy-saving of more than 16%. This paper technically explains the idea and the concrete methods in the successful technical challenge.

articleTitle: Fault-tolerant oriented control of modular linear switched-flux permanent magnet machine
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant control strategy for three phase linear switched-flux permanent magnet machine (LSFPMM) with modular structure, which has one-phase open-circuit fault. Under this condition, this three-phase LSFPMM has a novel perspective of the operating principle similar to two-phase machine. Based on finite element analysis (FEA), the performance of proposed fault-tolerant control strategy has been simulated. The predicted results show the fault-tolerant control strategy can effectively keep average thrust force and thrust ripple virtually unchanged after fault occurance. In addition, the influence of module gap on fault-tolerant performance has also been investigated. The larger module gap tends to improve fault-tolerant performance due to lower mutual inductances between phases, but decrease average force simultaneously. The proposed fault-tolerant control strategy can also be extended to other three-phase machines.

articleTitle: Operating characteristic of matrix converter for linear induction motor
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: In this paper, it is proposed to use a matrix converter for linear induction motor (LIM) drives. A matrix converter is a direct AC-AC converter. It has the potential to regenerate power and to connect directly across the AC power line, thus it is possible to improve the efficiency in the entire system of LIMs drive. In this experiments, the operating characteristics of the matrix converter were examined in the three states: acceleration, regeneration and direct connection when a LIM with a disc-shaped secondary side was driven. As a result, it is clear that the matrix converter is a suitable device for operating LIMs.

articleTitle: Thrust ripple reduction method of inner magnet linear synchronous motor
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: A thrust ripple reduction method for a permanent magnet linear synchronous motor is introduced. The mover consisting of a magnet, a ferromagnetic plate, and a back yoke is divided into three parts in the stacking direction. Each part is spatially displaced in the moving direction. The evaluation coefficient of the harmonic thrust similar to the distribution factor of the winding predicts the amount of the displacement for reducing the thrust ripple at the design stage. This method is compared with the case where the mover is skewed. Furthermore, it is estimated that both end parts of the back yoke act as to yield lower harmonic ripple.

articleTitle: Comparison of direct and indirectly liquid-cooled coreless linear actuators with multi-layer coils
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper describes the comparison between direct and indirectly liquid-cooled topologies for coreless linear motors with multiple coil layers. The electromagnetic force production is obtained by 3-D magnetic scalar potential modeling whereas thermal modeling is performed by 3-D finite element and volume methods. The power dissipation and force density of each topology is investigated for different pole pitches and wire configurations.

articleTitle: Sensorless method with parameter identification applied to a bistable fast linear switched reluctance actuator for textile machine
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper provides a sensorless method to control the position of keys passing through a linear actuator used in an industrial textile machine. The presented method describes how to find out the position of the key using two cascading discrete Kalman filters, the first for filtering the speed and the second for filtering the impedance measurement in other to retrieve the position. Due to the thickness difference from one textile machine to another, an actuator model, to evaluate impedance in function of position, is obtained by using parameter identification.

articleTitle: Magnetically levitated planar positioning systems based on Lorentz forces
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper presents a ironless actuator with two degrees of freedom (2-DoF), which generates a magnetic levitation and propulsion force. It is characterized by a very simple compact construction with a freely accessible mover from above. As a result, it provides a cost-effective solution for vacuum compatible high precision magnetically levitated planar systems. Two possible topology based on this actuation scheme will be shown and discussed. Fast and precise semi-analytical equations are derived in order to calculate the force components, generated by the magnetic guiding coil, as a function of the current mover position. Based on these equations, a geometrical optimization of the guiding coil is carried out in order to achieve maximum levitation force. The magnetic force components are calculated using the newly equations and are verified with three-dimensional finite element method (3D-FEM).

articleTitle: Gap-sensor-less electromagnetic suspension system using force sensor
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: When controlling the electromagnetic Suspension system, generally used the displacement sensor. But the Electromagnetic Suspension System using a displacement sensor accuracy of velocity calculation cause problems. This research theme is to solve this issue instead of using force sensor.

articleTitle: Load characteristics of a magnetically levitated system with hybrid magnets
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper reports the experimental results of the load characteristics of a magnetically levitated system with hybrid magnets, which we studied to replace street cars and conveyor systems. The new magnetically levitated system proposed here is low cost, easy to make, and energy saving. This system operates using AA-size dry-cell batteries. The application of pull-up-type magnetically levitated vehicles will be useful for free path track design and smooth running. The load experimental results are shown.

articleTitle: Novel oscillatory actuator for haptic device using principle of stepper motor
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: Mobile haptic devices are being studied extensively because they have great potential for use as information transfer devices. Amemiya et al. proposed a method for haptic feedback with a slider-crank mechanism that uses an asymmetrical drive. We have recently proposed a haptic device that uses a small two degree-of-freedom (2-DOF) oscillatory actuator. Using this actuator, we have investigated the relationship of the properties of the asymmetric acceleration to haptic perception by conducting experiments on volunteers. Then, by applying a genetic algorithm to the optimization method, we created an optimized asymmetric acceleration waveform. However it has a different oscillations in operating directions. In this report, we propose a new oscillatory actuator using stepper motor principle to realize uniform oscillations in different directions. We verify that the proposed actuator is able to generate an asymmetric acceleration waveform.

articleTitle: Arbitrarily close equilibrium orientations of magnetically levitated platforms
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: In this paper, the equilibrium orientations of magnetically suspended platforms that are statically loaded and constrained to 2 degrees of freedom are analyzed. It is shown that under these conditions, a symmetric, 2-magnet system can have a maximum of two equilibrium orientations for a given force-moment load. Further, it is shown that these two equilibrium orientations can exist arbitrarily close to each other under certain conditions. The conditions for arbitrarily close equilibrium orientations are analyzed, and verified to be physically achievable with numeric examples. The findings are presented as a consideration for acceptable operating loads for magnetically levitated platforms with zero-power control.

articleTitle: Basic study on linear actuator using superconducting coil
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: There are not so many cryogenic linear pumps, because linear pumps need a high power for driving themselves compared to centrifugal pumps. Then, we try to apply superconducting coil to a linear motor for cryogenic pump. Static and dynamic characteristics about the linear motor are discussed. The total linear motor system composed of the linear motor, a PID controller, a displacement sensor and a power amplifier. This paper discusses static and dynamic characteristics for the linear motor at room temperature and in liquid nitrogen. Step responses and follow-up control are performed in liquid nitrogen.

articleTitle: 3-D magnetic field analysis taking account of anisotropic magnetic hysteresis property of electrical steel sheet
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: We investigate whether an anisotropic magnetic hysteresis property can be obtained by 3-D numerical analysis. Two ring cores are prepared for the investigation: one is the ring stacked by the same rolling direction of electrical steel sheets, the other is the ring stacked by rotating the rolling direction. First, B-H properties and iron loss characteristics are obtained from actual measurement. Next, a validity of 3-D numerical analysis taking account of magnetic anisotropy and magnetic hysteresis at the same time is evaluated by comparing the experimental results. As a result, the numerical analysis results have the same tendency as the experimental results.

articleTitle: Improvement of evitation characteristics by the drive circuit in the magnetically levitated conveyance system using the linear stepper motor
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: The Conventional conveyance systems have problems such as vibration, noise and raising dust. Most system consists of the levitation (and guidance) section and the thrust one. In this research, by using the linear stepper motor, these sections are combined. The experimental device to realize this system has been made. Because the coil is controlled by high switching frequency for levitation, the improved drive circuit is created. This circuit is designed with circuit numerical analysis software and create the circuit based on the numerical analysis result. Characteristics of the created drive circuit shows good corresponding to the numerical analysis result. Difference of the attractive force between the attractive mode and the drop mode, becomes nine times as large as that of the previous circuit.

articleTitle: Consideration of linear synchronous motor characteristic in curved part
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: Linear synchronous motor (LSM) is used in industrial machines for positioning and conveying equipment. A variety of layout lines has been suggested to be highly expected to raise productivity. Flexible layout of the track including curved part is an advantage of the application. For example, the track shaped production lines of circular system is used to reduce the waste time that occurs during return and stop of the carrier including the mover. Furthermore, this paper discusses design considerations and verification results of Linear and Curvilinear Synchronous Motor (LCSM) which is a linear motor driving in a straight part and a curved part. It was confirmed that the ratio of the thrust reduction by FEM analysis and prototype evaluation are mostly the same as the result considering by skew factor. Moreover, Multi Carrier Module (MCM) demonstrated drive of LCSM seamlessly.

articleTitle: Evaluation on the effect of space factor of motor on torque characteristics
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: In this paper, we evaluate an effect of space factor of motor core on torque characteristics by using an interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM). 2-D magnetic field analysis changing the space factor of motor cores and current phase angle is carried out to clarify the effect of space factor. The results show that torque has a peak value in 76% space factor even if current phase angle is changed.

articleTitle: Development of a test stand for Maglev vehicles using hardware-in-the-loop simulation
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: A test stand consisting of one-third segment car body which simulates bending vibration is developed to evaluate ride comfort of maglev vehicles. The test stand utilizes hardware-in-the-loop simulation (HILS), which simulates motion of the missing segment using numerical simulation. Experimental results confirm that the test stand with the HILS system can generate the bending vibration accurately. Then, a method to reduce the bending vibration is proposed. Fundamental experiments using the test stand indicate that the optimally-designed anchor, a coupling element between the car body and the bogie, can reduce the bending vibration. It is expected that this test stand will lead to improvement of ride comfort of maglev vehicles.

articleTitle: Improvement of the magnetic circuit of the rotor using the raibach array and iron in the RTS magnetic bearing
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: The magnetic bearing using the high temperature bulk superconductor (HTS) has been developed. In this system, the ring shaped permanent magnet is installed in the rotor. It has two poles. This configuration realizes increment of the linkage flux of the surface of the HTS on the stator. Pinning force of the HTS is used to support the rotor weight and keep the rotor stability. Pinning force depends on amount of the linkage flux of the HTS. The flux of the rotor is not used sufficiently in the conventional model. So, the rotor with halbach array and the combined iron model are considered. In this halbach array model, the flux of the rotor is concentrated toward the HTS. The flux of the combined iron model is compared with the model without iron. The flux of the horizontal direction and the vertical direction increase by 22.12% and 3.03% respectively.

articleTitle: Evaluation system of reactor iron loss under PWM inverter excitation
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: Reactor iron loss was evaluated under inverter excitation using LC parallel resonance circuit. LC parallel resonance was used to supply a higher current than the limitation of the power source. Experimental results showed that there was a difference in ring iron loss, but there was no difference in reactor iron loss between sinusoidal excitation and inverter excitation. The reason why there is no difference in loss in the reactor is that the carrier harmonic component becomes relatively small. This means that the influence of the harmonic component on the core loss is small.

articleTitle: Prototype of magnetic energy harvesting device as a 3.3 V battery
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to obtain power for driving sensors using the magnetic energy harvesting. The magnetic energy harvesting device is constituted with a coil, a full-wave rectifier circuit and a DC-DC step-down converter. In this paper, this device was evaluated to obtain a DC output voltage of 3.3 V. Additionary, a target power for driving sensors was set to 90 mW. As an evaluated result, an output voltage of 3.3 V could be obtained. Especially, a output power of 104 mW harvested at connected a load resistance of 100 Ω.

articleTitle: Experimental study on iron loss properties of an amorphous ring under different inverter excitations
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This study focuses on an evaluation of iron losses of an amorphous ring under different inverter excitations. We examine the iron loss characteristics as a function of carrier frequency under Si-IGBT- and GaN-FET-inverter excitations. The ring test under GaN-FET-inverter excitation at high carrier frequency shows drastically large iron loss compared with that excited by Si-IGBT-inverter because of the ringing derived from the high speed switching.

articleTitle: High-force linear iron-core fine-tooth motor
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper presents the design and testing of a high force linear fine-tooth iron-core permanent magnet motor. We present the design and experimental results in comparison with a commercially-available iron-core linear motor. Our new fine-tooth motor shows predicted shear stress improvements of 28 % at the prototype practical power level of 10 W/mm and 85 % at an anticipated ultimate root mean square (RMS) current density limit in the coil wires of 50 A/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, relative to the conventional iron-core motor. This force performance of our new motor is also experimentally validated. The new motor shows strong potential for industry applications requiring precision motion along with high speed of production, such as in photo-lithography machines.

articleTitle: Linear oscillatory actuator integrated with magnetic gear for E-cutter development
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper proposes a linear oscillatory actuator integrated with a magnetic gear for E-cutter development to harvest oil palm fresh fruit bunch (FFB). The machine comprises of a linear magnetic gear which is artfully integrated with a slotless linear motor. The idea is proposed to improve the performance of existing linear actuators. The design is targeted for a optimum motor thrust, light weight, low cycle time, and reliable displacement. Most importantly, the direction of motion for both the linear motor and linear magnetic gear is opposite to each other, and this could reduce the vibration disturbance from the machine. The performance of the proposed machine is analyzed by finite element method (FEM) and the simulation results verify the machine design.

articleTitle: Development of a noncontact impact relieving device of a falling object by electromagnetic impulsive force
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: This paper introduces a noncontact impact relieving device of a falling object by electromagnetic impulsive force. The device consists of a conductive plate, a coil and a drive circuit which contains high voltage power supply, capacitor and electrical switches. By discharging capacitor charge into the coil, eddy current is induced to the conductive plate located near the coil. Then, the electromagnetic interaction of the eddy current and coil current generates impulsive repulsive force. This force allows the falling object to avoid high-speed collision with land without mechanical contact. In this paper, an experimental equipment and results of fall tests are shown. The results demonstrate that the proposed device is effective to reduce landing impact.

articleTitle: Analytical modelling techniques for thrust force calculation of a permanent magnet linear motor
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)

authors.preferredName: D. T. E. H. van Casteren

abstract: This paper presents a comparative study on two analytical modelling techniques (i.e. Fourier analysis and Tooth Contour Method), applied to a benchmark topology of a linear permanent magnet synchronous motor (LPMSM). The investigated methods are used for obtaining the thrust force of a LPMSM with significantly reduced computation time (from the order of seconds to the order of milliseconds), compared to traditional numerical modelling techniques (i.e. Finite elements method). Despite the reduced computation time, the analytical modelling techniques accuracy is kept high, having less than 5.0% discrepancy, in comparison to the finite elements method.

articleTitle: The development of criteria for evaluating energy efficiency and the choice of the optimal composition of the subsystems in the Russian integral transit transport system
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: The paper focuses on the potential of the Russian Federation that has been `ordained' by its advantageous location and geographical position to play the role of the international transport transit corridor. To solve this fundamental task the authors suggest creating a unified integral transit transport system. On the basis of optimal transport multimodality and the concept of high-speed trans- and ultrasonic land vacuum maglev transport (VMLT) this system is supposed to integrate the whole complex of both existing and future innovative means of transport (`atmospheric', maglev, flying boats, underwater, ground effect vehicles, flying containers, airships, ESTOLAS, etc.). In the integral transit transport system vacuum VMLT principle can serve as a basis for implementing a number of economically efficient and breakthrough transport business concepts and technologies. Different transport systems are compared in terms of an integral transport system.

articleTitle: Origin of magnetism — 90 Years of misunderstanding
publicationTitle: 2017 11th International Symposium on Linear Drives for Industry Applications (LDIA)
abstract: Most of the people recall their interest in science during their student days where they would collect iron present in the sand using a horseshoe magnet and observe peculiar patterns called lines of magnetic force. However, they lose their way while trying to understand magnetism. They were taught that there are N and S poles at the ends of a magnet. When cut into two pieces, once again N and S poles appear on the ends of each of the pieces. Even if the process of cutting the magnet continues, we still obtain N and S poles at the ends of each piece. In order to understand this, several questions of fundamental nature arise in the minds of clever students: To begin with, what are N and S poles? Are there only N or S poles? What are the lines of magnetic force? The general response from many teachers to these questions would be that the magnet is a material without any deep understanding. With such an off-handed argument, such students understand that science is a subject of categorization and its concepts, required to be memorized in order to obtain good grades. With such a belief, they begin to dislike science, and find that it is difficult to understand concepts this way.
